headline: Red Sox show some fight in Detroit while the legal dust settles
morning_brew: Tuesday night in Detroit was exactly what this team needed to build some momentum. Ten runs on twelve hits was a sight for sore eyes after that rough stretch we saw at Fenway Park earlier this month. Ceddanne Rafaela was the man of the hour, driving in four runs and launching a massive home run to break things open. The real fireworks happened in the fourth when Framber Valdez decided to drill Trevor Story, leading to the benches clearing and an ejection. Hear me out before you laugh, but seeing the guys stand up for each other like that shows a grit we have been missing lately.

Jaylen Brown is lighter in the wallet today after the league handed down a fifty thousand dollar fine for his comments about the officiating. It is a tough pill to swallow after that first-round exit at the Garden, but the league office does not play around when you question the integrity of the game. We are stuck watching the rest of the NBA playoffs from the couch while teams like the Timberwolves and Knicks keep grinding. It is going to be a long summer of looking at the lottery and free agency lists to see how this roster gets back to chasing Banner 19. The Hub feels a little quieter without green on the floor in May.

The legal process wrapped up for Stefon Diggs with a not guilty verdict on all counts yesterday. It is a relief for everyone to have a resolution so the focus can eventually return to the field. We will see what the league decides regarding any further review of the situation under the personal conduct policy. If he is available for the full season, he is going to be a massive part of a squad that won fourteen games last fall. We need every weapon we can get to stay competitive in a crowded AFC field as we look toward training camp in Foxborough.

news_digest.headline: Celtics' Jaylen Brown fined $50,000 for criticizing officials
news_digest.dans_take: That is a steep price to pay for speaking your mind after a tough loss.

news_digest.headline: Jury finds Stefon Diggs not guilty of assault, strangulation
news_digest.dans_take: Glad to see a resolution in court, now we wait for the league to finish their review.

news_digest.dans_take: Always good to keep an eye on the next wave of talent for the B's.
